newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks set all-time high, end at record.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks set all-time high, end at record.

text.p: Swiss shares closed with a record high on Monday in a session that also saw a new all-time high of 4,756.3 points on the blue-chip SMI index.
The market was characterised by selective buying, dealers said, adding the positive development of some shares supported the market. Dealers also observed growing foreign demand.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) rose 41 points or 0.87 percent to 4,740.1 points.
The broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) added 21.8 points or 0.71 percent at 2990.30 points.
Roche and Novartis dominated the market. Roche recovered after last week's heavy losses and jumped 395 francs, or 3.5 percent, to 11,900.
Novartis suffered from profit-taking and dropped five francs to 1885.
Nestle was also among the volume leaders. The stock ended six francs higher at 1,774.
ABB ended higher 39 francs at 1,748 before the release of first quarter figures on Tuesday.

Swiss Re closed 35 francs higher at 1,587 after a Swiss newspaper said the company planned to set up its alternate risk business as a separate legal entity, possibly paving the way for a joint venture in this growing sector, dealers said.
A Swiss Re spokesman confirmed "that we are thinking along those lines" but would only say the company planned to issue a statement on this issue on April 28.
Winterthur and CS Group, which are often mentioned in connection with bancassurance ventures at Swiss Re, closed hardly changed. Both companies have product cooperation with Swsis Re already.
Zurich and SBC showed solid gains. Zurich gained 3.5 francs to end at 458.5. SBC added 6.0 francs to close at 305.5.
